top_choice_rationale: Base editing turns a defined enzymatic reaction, deamination of a nucleobase in DNA, into a programmable single-base conversion without double-strand cleavage. The adenine editor required an activity that does not exist in nature and had to be evolved, so the achievement is a new chemical capability and not a repackaging of Cas9 cleavage (2020 prize). It has been reproduced in very many independent laboratories for about a decade and has reached first-in-human use. The Liu/Komor/Gaudelli allocation follows the documented lineage of the cytosine and adenine editors, though it leaves out Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID), and the citation should be kept to the 2016-2017 discovery.
